study: Decoding demand: the appetite for alternative proteins in Southeast Asia
lead_org_or_authors: The Good Growth Co. for GFI APAC (authors cited as J. Morton, D. Gandhi, E. Wong)
countries: Vietnam, Thailand, Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore
sample_frame: Online panel; capital-city regions plus Ho Chi Minh City for Vietnam; adults (18-24 is the youngest reported band); not nationally representative
method: Desk research and market visits; online focus groups (8 people per country who were reducing meat); quantitative online survey; six segments
key_question_wording: What is your familiarity with plant-based meat? (5 options from never heard to eat regularly, one or more times per week). What would make you eat more plant-based meat? (rank up to 3). How often would you choose plant-based meat if all your concerns are resolved? Imagine you were doing your grocery shopping and the following products were available that would suit the dish you were wanting to cook. Which would you purchase? (plant-based meat, meat, neither), repeated at -20%, same, +20%, +50%, +100% price
key_vn_results: Heard of PBM 90%; ever tried 42%; eat monthly or more 20%; weekly 3%. Intend to reduce meat 15% (lowest of six). Would choose PBM over meat: 88% at 20% cheaper, 74% at parity, 64% at +20%, 47% at +50%, 26% at +100%. Top factors to eat more: affordable 38%, nutritious 36%, more available when shopping 31%, tasted better 30%, more variety 29%, fewer additives 27%. Blends: 55% very, 40% slightly interested. Curious segment 43% of Vietnam sample
regional_or_peer_comparison: Six-country average: heard 91%, tried 47%, weekly 5%; reduce meat 21%; parity 62%, +20% 47%; affordable 47%. Vietnam highest stated purchase at parity, +20% and +50%
quality_reason: Large per-country online sample with published question wording and per-country n for key charts; full report gated; commissioned by an advocacy group; urban online frame
notes: Regional headline 5% to 63% refers to weekly eaters now (5%) versus always or often if all concerns resolved (15% plus 48%); no Vietnam split published for that item

study: Plant-based food alternatives: future or present?
lead_org_or_authors: Rakuten Insight
countries: 13 markets incl. Vietnam, Thailand, Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore
sample_frame: Rakuten Insight proprietary online panel; men and women aged 16+
key_question_wording: Have you ever consumed plant-based alternatives to animal-based food products (such as nut or rice milk, cheeses made from nuts, plant-based burger patties or sausages, vegan gummi bears, etc.)?
key_vn_results: Ever consumed 86% (highest of 13). Of Vietnamese triers: plant milk 87%, plant-based meat alternatives 49%, dairy substitutes 46%. Reasons: healthier 61%, animal welfare 40%, vegetarian or vegan diet 38%, trend 36%. Barriers: hard to find 39%, taste 29%, cost 24%, unsure of ingredients 24%. Frequency: several times a week 44%
regional_or_peer_comparison: Ever consumed: Thailand 73%, Indonesia 73%, Malaysia 68%, Philippines 65%, Singapore 61%
product_scope: All plant-based alternatives, dominated by plant milk; mock meats may include traditional do chay
quality_reason: Large online panel; category definition broad; method note minimal; no weighting described
notes: Total n = 124,100 APAC plus 5,900 US

study: Swiss and Vietnamese meat consumer segmentation (also Ha et al. 2024 Meat Science; Giacomuzzo et al. 2024 on vegetables use the same survey)
lead_org_or_authors: Bern University of Applied Sciences and Vietnam National University of Agriculture (Delley, Ha, Götze and others)
funder: Swiss National Science Foundation and NAFOSTED (joint award IZVSZ1_203324)
sample_frame: Urban residents 18+ in Hanoi, Hai Phong, Ho Chi Minh City; snowball via companies, consumer and parent associations on Zalo and Facebook; 77% university-educated, 59% women; non-meat eaters excluded
method: Online survey; cluster analysis on 9 psychographic scales
key_question_wording: Six-point scales on meat safety concern, meat attachment, health risk, self-efficacy, familial influence, intention to reduce, animal welfare, environment, local and seasonal food; How important is it that the food you eat on a typical day is nutritious, affordable, good for health, very safe, in line with my culture
key_vn_results: Flexitarian 4%; 0.74 kg meat per week. Segments: anxious 26%, suggestible 25%, meat lovers 19%, confident 16%, proactive 14%. Importance (1 to 6): good for health 5.40, very high food safety 5.35, nutritious 5.23, affordable 4.96, in line with culture 4.39. Proactive reducers skew to the two lowest income bands
regional_or_peer_comparison: Switzerland: 34% flexitarian; 0.51 to 0.55 kg meat per week; price and meat safety much less important
quality_reason: Peer-reviewed, open data description, clear frame; snowball sample skewed to educated urban workers
notes: Best academic evidence on Vietnamese meat-reduction psychology; does not measure plant-based products

study: Healthy or environmentally friendly? Meat practices of green consumers
lead_org_or_authors: Markoni, Ha, Götze and others

sample_frame: Self-identified green consumers; online group discussions
key_vn_results: Vietnamese decisions driven by health and food safety (fear of hormones in meat); meat is non-negotiable at special-occasion meals; family influence strong; red meat swapped for white meat
quality_reason: Qualitative, small, green-consumer frame

study: How to message plant-based diets and products in Southeast Asia: a social media analysis
lead_org_or_authors: Good Growth, Faunalytics, Mercy For Animals
sample_frame: Public posts on X; English plus local keywords (Vietnam: +chay, thuần thực vật, dựa trên thực vật)
key_vn_results: Vietnam: top motivations health, animal protection, environment; barriers too few to rank (5.5% of barrier mentions); about 3.4% of Vietnamese and Indonesian posts mention cutting meat because of prices
regional_or_peer_comparison: Region: barriers health concerns 22.8%, cost 16.2%, culture and religion 12.0%, negative views of advocates 9.6%, over-processing 8.4% of mentions
quality_reason: X is marginal in Vietnam (Facebook, Zalo and TikTok dominate); 73 posts
notes: Online talk is behaviour of a kind (what people post), not purchasing

study: Consumer insights and alternative protein-rich products from alcoholic beverage by-products (RD-32)
lead_org_or_authors: Nguyen M.Q., Nguyen T.T., Nguyen T.C. (HUST)
sample_frame: Google Forms, aged 18 to 25 in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City; convenience
method: Online survey plus sensory test (51 HUST students, 19 to 24) of three energy bars
key_question_wording: Willingness to try a new energy bar using alternative protein from safe by-products of alcoholic beverage production
key_vn_results: 84% aware of alternative protein products but not used (as reported); 46% willing to try the by-product energy bar; top concerns flavour, safety, price; best bar overall acceptability 4.45 on a 1 to 7 hedonic scale
regional_or_peer_comparison: Compared by authors with 56% US willingness to try biomass protein
quality_reason: Small convenience student sample; awareness figure identical to SUR-10
notes: Sensory part is tested but has no price element

study: Willingness to try novel alternative protein products in Hanoi
lead_org_or_authors: Nguyen M.Q., Nguyen T.N.M., Nguyen T.C., Vu H.S., Luong T.H. and others (HUST)
sample_frame: Aged 18 to 25 in Hanoi; structured questionnaire; 3 focus groups of 20
key_question_wording: Price items: The price of alternative protein products is higher than that of conventional ones; The higher price of NAP products prevents me from buying them. WTT1: I am willing to pay a high price for NAP products
key_vn_results: Text states 84% aware but not used; sample text says 202 of 288 (70%). Awareness via social media 47.9%, e-commerce 22.7%. Health concern strongest driver of attitude; subjective norms strongest driver of willingness to try; price negative
product_scope: Novel alternative protein (plant and yeast named)
quality_reason: Small youth sample; internal inconsistency in the key descriptive

study: Behavioural drivers of plant-based food consumption intention among urban youth, Hanoi

sample_frame: University students in Hanoi; Google Forms snowball plus intercepts at vegetarian restaurants and campuses; 70.6% earn under VND 3 million a month
key_question_wording: Religious belief items such as: My religious beliefs dictate that I must eat a vegetarian diet
key_vn_results: Health consciousness strongest (beta 0.474), social norms (0.350), animal welfare (0.118); environmental concern negative (-0.092); religion not significant. Purchase intention: occasionally 83.3%, frequently 3.3%, never 13.5%
quality_reason: Small convenience sample; implausible spending item (68.6% claim VND 0.5 to 1 million a month on plant-based food)
